column1: # lib/coding-agents.tsv — the coding agents whose live sessions are never touched.
# ONE list, read by both sides: `lib/live-sessions.sh` (the cleaners' exemption)
# and the app's `CodingAgentHosts` (what Monitor locks and the cleanup review
# keeps). A session's ROOT is a running program that matches one of these
# lines; every process that descends from a root belongs to the session.
# `agent-runner --probe-agents` fails if the two sides ever disagree.
# An agent that is NOT listed here is NOT protected: its sessions look like any
# other dev tooling. Add a line to protect one. A list that is missing, empty
# or unreadable protects nothing, so both sides refuse to act at all (they fail closed).
#   kind  exe       the executable's file name is exactly `text`
#         fragment  `text` (plain text, not a pattern) is in the PROGRAM'S OWN PATH: the
#                   executable, or for an interpreter launch (`node script.js`) the script.
#                   A command that only MENTIONS the text in its arguments (`tail -f
#                   the command line must contain that too.
#         ignore    the executable is never a session root (a search helper)
#         interpreter  the executable runs a script named in its arguments, so the script
#                   (first argument that is not a flag) counts as the program's own path
#         container    an app that runs containers or virtual machines, whose processes
#                   macOS cannot see: quitting it ends whatever runs inside (the agent
#                   column is "-"; the text is the app's name)
